pages.hook: A neighborhood bakery in Brooklyn smells like warm bread and sugar. Learn the words you need to ask the price, choose and pay.

mythfact.s: In the USA, the price on a shelf usually does not include sales tax.
mythfact.why: In most states, sales tax is added when you pay.

mythfact.s: Bakeries only sell bread.
mythfact.why: Most also sell cookies, cakes, croissants and coffee.

mythfact.s: Brooklyn is a part of New York City.
mythfact.why: Brooklyn is one of the five boroughs of New York City.

mythfact.s: You say “a bread” to ask for one loaf.
mythfact.why: Bread is uncountable. Say “a loaf of bread”.

mythfact.s: “The Little Red Hen” is a folk tale with no known author.
mythfact.why: It comes from oral tradition and many people tell it.

compare.br: In Brazil, the padaria is part of daily life: people go early for pão francês and coffee, often buying by unit or by weight.
compare.us: In the USA, many people buy a whole loaf, or a few cookies, and the shop may be smaller and more focused on sweets.
compare.tip: To count bread, use “a loaf of bread”, “two loaves of bread”.
compare.ask: What do you buy at the bakery? Say it in English.

quiz.q: You want to know the price of the bread. You say…
quiz.why: How much is…? asks for a price.

quiz.q: You want one loaf. You say…
quiz.why: I’ll take one, please is natural.

opts: pay and say Here you go
quiz.why: Give the money and say Here you go.

pages.title: Reading quest — A loaf for Anya · part 1
text: Anya lives in **Brooklyn**. On Saturday, she wants to make a sandwich for her little brother. She needs one thing: fresh bread. She goes to the bakery on her street.

The bakery is warm and smells sweet. Ava works at the counter. “Hi! **Can I help you?**” she asks. Anya says, “Yes. **How much is the bread?**” “**Four dollars a loaf**,” says Ava. “**I’ll take one, please.**”
“**Anything else?** The cookies are **fresh**,” says Ava. Anya looks at the cakes, the croissants and the cookies. They all look great. “**Two cookies, please**,” she says. “**That’s six dollars.**”

opts: A girl buys bread and cookies
fast.why: Anya buys bread and two cookies.

pages.title: Reading quest — A loaf for Anya · part 2
text: Anya gives Ava the money. “**Here you go. Thanks!**” “**Have a sweet day!**” says Ava. Anya smiles and leaves with a loaf of bread and two cookies.

At home, Anya remembers the story of the Little Red Hen. The hen makes flour and then bread, all alone. Anya is lucky: she only needs a few dollars and a short walk. She shares a cookie with her brother. “You bet it’s good!” he says.

errors.why: Bread is uncountable. Use a loaf of.
More than one noun needs -s.
The price pattern is It’s … dollars a loaf.

pages.title: Boss mission — At the bakery

brief.teacher: You are Ava. Change the plan during the scene.
brief.student: You are at a bakery in Brooklyn. Ava works at the counter. Buy bread and cookies. You are the customer / visitor.

orders: I need a bag of flour.
complications: The other person did not hear you: repeat.

pages.title: Free production
pages.prompt: Você está no mercado. Peça um pacote de farinha, um pão e uma caixa de açúcar. Ligue à referência The Little Red Hen: abre a situação para praticar “pedir comida pela embalagem: a bag of flour, a loaf of bread, a box of sugar”.
pages.model: A bag of flour, a loaf of bread and a box of sugar, please. The Little Red Hen helps here.

tasks.name: Say it
tasks.prompt: Preciso de um pacote de farinha.
tasks.model: I need a bag of flour.

items: Record yourself asking How much is…?
Listen to the dialogue again and shadow Ava.
Review: a loaf of / a bag of / a box of.

pages.title: Mission complete
recap: I need a bag of flour.
Preciso de um pacote de farinha.
I want a loaf of bread.
Yes. How much is the bread?
pages.homework: Write a short price list for your own bakery and say it aloud in English.
